summary.text: 山 is a pictograph of mountain peaks standing together; its common meaning is “mountain.”

formation.text: 山 is a whole-graph pictograph of mountain peaks, not a compound of separate semantic or phonetic parts. Shang oracle-bone outlines and varied Shang and Western Zhou bronze depictions are described, alongside later listed script forms.

components.text: The whole graph 山 depicts mountain peaks standing together; it is an indivisible pictorial form, not a set of smaller components.

history.text: Shang oracle-bone forms are described as mountain outlines. Shang and Western Zhou bronze forms vary, showing three or five peaks, either filled or outlined; later forms are described as stylized. The listed script stages do not establish a continuous sequence of graphic changes. The selected small-seal-style image is a modern redraw, not an ancient specimen.

A Han-period dictionary account says that 山 disperses qi, gives rise to the myriad things, and is high with rocks, then labels the graph pictographic. This is a historical interpretation, not confirmation of the graph’s original meaning.

uncertainties.text: The available account does not establish the date or lexical value of the earliest specimen, precise dates for the listed forms, or a continuous graphic development.

senses.text: The landscape-noun sense is supported in early inscriptional and literary contexts and remains an ordinary current meaning. Its earliest attestation and deeper chronology are unresolved.

limitations.text: The 《合集》96 reading and its proposed gloss about sacrifice to the nine mountains remain tentative. The 《詩經》 examples support landscape use, but the poem’s composition date and earliest physical witness are unresolved. The reviewed evidence establishes no semantic transition.

relationships.text: The landscape-noun sense is supported in early inscriptional and literary contexts and remains an ordinary current meaning. Its earliest attestation and deeper chronology are unresolved.

overview.text: 山 pictures mountain peaks standing together and commonly means “mountain.”

components.text: The whole character pictures mountain peaks standing together.

items.period: Seal-script tradition; the file depicts a Shuowen seal-style form, without a specimen date
items.caption: This modern redraw of 山 in small-seal style shows three upright peaks joined by a curved base, illustrating the mountain-like pictograph in a seal-script form.
items.alt: A black small-seal form of 山: three tall upright strokes rise from a rounded, curved base.
items.selection_reason: It clearly illustrates the seal-script stage listed in the paleographic record and the pictographic interpretation of 山 as mountain peaks.
